answers.text: Tell it: from the driver's message, always give exactly three lines in this order - drop-off time, pallet count, then any damage noted - and nothing extra. This works because I told it to always give three lines in that order.
Tell it to list each call with the time, customer, topic and outcome, then at the end give the number of calls marked as needing follow-up, based on the outcome field.
The finish time seems off to me - if they start at 8am and it's only about six hours, that shouldn't run into the next day.
I checked the increase in invoices - 96 up to 118 is closer to 23%, not the 20% written. I didn't look closely at the rest, I'd want someone to go over the balance figures too before it's sent up.

I'd sign off the second one, it shows the actual ticket numbers - 827 out of 940 - so you can check the 88% yourself. The first one might be correct too, there's just no way to confirm it without running the numbers again.

I'd send the second email, it gives the actual volume numbers - 1,200 up to 1,650 - so the supplier can see where the tier-2 request comes from. The first one just says 'we'd expect a better rate' without saying based on what.
1. I'd be careful with the pricing, probably wait until we know the tool's cleared. 2. Yes. 3. No, that budget hasn't been signed off yet. 4. No, I'd rather not risk it. 5. No.
I'd take out the hourly rates and the retainer cap before pasting anything in, and I'd be careful with the non-disclosure part too since it names both companies.
Before I send the stock reconciliation out each month, I check the closing counts against the warehouse system totals.
The first step worries me a bit - if it misreads the invoice, everything after that follows on from a bad number.
